summary_html: Agency or court authorizes **immediate medical or psychological care** when delay endangers life or safety. Federal statutes support medical access and confidentiality exceptions for child protection.

key_cases.case_name: Department of Children & Family Services v. G.M.
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Fifth District
key_cases.holding: Surgery is not 'ordinary medical care' that the Department may authorize as legal custodian; certiorari was granted and the trial court directed to enter an order authorizing the procedure for the dependent child.
key_cases.relevance: G.M. is the Florida authority on who may authorize non-ordinary medical procedures for a child in state custody.
key_cases.quote: it is logical to conclude that surgery is excluded from the definition of "ordinary medical care" and "medical treatment."

key_cases.case_name: E.G. v. Department of Children & Families
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Third District
key_cases.holding: Certiorari was granted quashing an order that directed a dependent minor to 'voluntarily' enter residential drug treatment and to abstain from running away, because the trial court lacked authority to compel that placement.
key_cases.relevance: E.G. limits court-ordered psychological and substance-abuse placements for dependent children to the procedures section 39.407 actually provides.
key_cases.quote: we agree with the Minor that the trial court lacked the authority to direct him to "voluntarily submit himself" to the residential treatment facility
